artboards.title: HUD · night · type A: Chakra Petch + Share Tech Mono
HUD · night · type B: Martian Mono everywhere

annotations.text:
ROUND 4 — back to the HUD, keeping the tiling bones.

Square everything: chamfered panels, corner brackets, 1px rules, diamond nodes and orthogonal edges in the graph. Cyan = system / ready, magenta = needs a human or is live, amber = draft only. Warmth comes from copy and pacing, not from softening the geometry.

Two type options, same layout: A Chakra Petch (squared humanist) + Share Tech Mono; B Martian Mono, a wide techno mono for everything. Pick one; both day/wide boards use A for now.

Row 2 — the other surfaces, all night / type A.

Kanban: columns are the lifecycle; human-only transitions are marked so a drag the controller owns is refused, not faked.

Ticket: spec + planning conversation side by side; state rail on the right; runs/history below it.

Project: outcomes up top (what survived, not what shipped), design revisions as path+sha, the ticket table.
Motion: scanline over the live run, the running node pulses, cursor blinks, focused tile glows inward. All off under reduced-motion.

TUI investigation — the same home and ticket screens as a full-screen terminal app (168×48, box-drawing, 3 accent colours, same keys as the GUI).

What survives: the tiles, the attention list, the claim order, the run meters, the planning conversation. What suffers: the dependency graph (hand-drawn ASCII, unmaintainable past ~15 nodes), drag-and-drop (becomes J/K reorder), and the 32" case (a TUI just gets wider columns).

A TUI could be the first client the blueprint's S1 calls "minimal" — the web GUI the second.
